answers.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's warriors plus buildings in the clearing; tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule and cannot stop another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: ‘warriors plus buildings’; ‘Tokens and pawns do not contribute.’

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the player's warriors or pawns from a clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. The mover must rule the origin, destination, or both, and rule is checked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answers.evidence: Move (4.2): ‘any positive number’; rule one end; ‘move the same pieces repeatedly’; rivers are not paths.

answers.answer: 1. Ambush: defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's card is discarded; a foiled ambush gives no hits. If not foiled, defender immediately deals two hits, then discards it; if no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not capped by defending warriors. 2. Resolve before-roll effects; if both sides have them, attacker orders them. 3. Roll: higher die gives attacker's rolled hits and lower gives defender's (ties equal); each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defense reverses dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords rather than warriors. 4. Resolve after-roll effects, attacker choosing order if both have effects. 5. Count hits by adding extra hits without warrior caps and subtracting ignored hits; if defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless extra hit (Vagabond is defenseless with no undamaged swords). 6. Each side removes one opposing piece per hit. The side taking hits chooses removal order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens, and orders effects triggered by its own removals. Both sides deal counted hits; losing warriors does not alter the roll cap retroactively. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores one VP each, including a defender and removals outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3), six enumerated steps; removal paragraph states warrior priority and removal VP.

answers.answer: Crafting cost is the card's bottom-left crafting icons; activate one matching crafting piece per icon, and the card's suit is not the crafting cost. Each crafting piece can activate once per turn, except Vagabond can reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. If an item card's item is absent from the map supply, it cannot be crafted. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Craft (4.1): icons define cost; once per turn exception; item card needs map supply; duplicate persistent effect prohibited.

answers.answer: In the player's own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand; remove the score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of that player's Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins by ruling three clearings of the matching suit; bird dominance wins by ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced, and cannot be discarded.
answers.evidence: Dominance (3.3): own Daylight at ‘at least 10 VP’; conditions checked at start of own Birdsong; ‘Cannot remove/replace activated card.’

answers.answer: When a dominance card is spent for suit, it goes near the map as an available card instead of into discard. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into hand. An available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card may pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking it and activating it are separate, and neither requires a faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Dominance: ‘Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available’; available bird ‘payment must be bird.’

answers.answer: With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover all four R building slots with ruins. Put the map item supply (2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins) on its corresponding spaces. Keep four R-marked ruin items separate; only if Vagabond is in play, hide one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword under the four ruins, one under each; without Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Factions set up in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–7 and faction setup sections: two-player deck rule, ruins/items, letter order.

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to put those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this applies outside battle too. Field Hospitals have no destination if the Keep is absent. The Keep cannot be placed again once removed.
answers.evidence: Marquise → Keep: placement ban and move permission; Field Hospitals card and destination; ‘cannot be placed again.’

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight begins by crafting with workshops, then permits up to three actions plus one action per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. March is one compound action consisting of up to two moves; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be done only once per turn; if supply is short, place the maximum available among eligible recruiters. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise Daylight: craft then actions; March, Recruit, Overwork procedures.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost printed atop that column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Building is illegal if full wood cost, building, rule, or legal slot is missing.
answers.evidence: Marquise Daylight → Build: rule/open slot, leftmost building, linked ruled wood network, VP on uncovered space.

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong in order: (1) Emergency Orders: if hand is empty, draw one card. (2) Add one or two hand cards to Decree, with at most one added bird card; each may go in any column, with no column size limit. (3) A New Roost: if there are no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can legally be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Birdsong numbered steps; New Roost requires fewest-warrior clearing where all pieces can be placed.

answers.answer: Craft first using roosts, then resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit → Move → Battle → Build order; within a column, choose card order freely, and bird is wild. Recruit places one warrior at one chosen roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic). Move at least one warrior from a matching clearing using normal move rules. Battle in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rule, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be completed fully, enter Turmoil immediately; do not skip it or continue to another column.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Daylight → resolve Decree; four required action descriptions and immediate Turmoil rule.

answers.answer: Turmoil: lose one VP per bird Decree card, counting both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none is face up, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends, then take the full normal Evening: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
answers.evidence: Turmoil, in order: bird-card VP loss including Viziers, discard/leader/Vizier steps, full Evening, map pieces remain.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one hand card matching that clearing (birds count) to Supporters; a group movement is one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to Alliance and Alliance draws one card from the deck into Supporters. If the Supporters stack is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; the payment or no-match draw still happens.
answers.evidence: Alliance → Outrage states triggers, payment per move, no-match procedure, and full-stack handling.

answers.answer: Order/timing: finish all Revolts before beginning Spread Sympathy; after spreading starts, no return to Revolt that Birdsong. Revolt eligibility: choose a sympathetic clearing with no base that matches a base still on Alliance board; spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token removed, place matching base, then warriors equal to sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit and one in Officers box. Spread Sympathy eligibility: choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; pay matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token. Martial Law adds one matching supporter if at least three warriors belonging to one other player are there. Place sympathy and score uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep placement ban still applies.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong: all Revolts before Spread Sympathy; separate procedures, eligibility, costs and results.

answers.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one warrior from supply in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Officers determine the number of Evening military operations. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score its uncovered VP; it needs legal token placement but no supporters, adjacency, or Martial Law payment. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Losing a base; Daylight Train; Organize and Evening operation rules.

answers.answer: Refresh in Birdsong: count tea already face up on the Refresh track; flip two exhausted items face up per such tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed now does not add refreshes in this step. Optional Slip then moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors; ignore effects preventing movement out of a clearing. A normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; ignore rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. Hostile warriors trigger the extra boot, buildings/tokens alone do not. In Evening, if in a forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; then Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest, discards to five, and checks capacity.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Birdsong Refresh/Slip; Daylight Move; Evening four steps and card drawing.

answers.answer: Explore: exhaust a torch in a ruin's clearing, take one hidden item face up into Satchel or its matching track, and score one VP if an item is taken; removing the last item removes the ruin and frees the building slot. Quest: in a matching clearing, select a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, and put it in the completed play area; choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards, then display a replacement quest. Repair: exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel without changing its face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space. Damaging moves an item to Damaged box without changing its face; item face (ready/exhausted) and damage are separate states.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight Explore, Quest, Repair; Pawn and items damage/face rules.

answers.answer: A faction becomes Hostile immediately when Vagabond removes one of its warriors while it is non-Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. During battle on Vagabond's own turn, Infamy gives one extra VP per hostile piece removed except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; hostile buildings/tokens thus normally give two total VP (one removal VP plus Infamy), and later hostile warriors give one Infamy VP. No Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, although Aid may still obtain an item; coalition with a Hostile faction resets it to Indifferent. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors there may it instead remove another faction piece. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Relationships → Hostile/Infamy and Daylight Strike; coalition Hostile reset.

answers.answer: Coalition is available to Vagabond only with four or more players. During Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card to coalition with a player not already in a coalition, whose VP is lowest among all players other than Vagabond; choose among tied lowest players. Put Vagabond's score marker on the partner's faction board and stop scoring. Vagabond wins if partner wins, including by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition (9.2.8), including player count, timing, selection, victory, relationship effects.

answers.answer: A card overrides the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. General and faction rules are applied together where possible; if incompatible, the faction rule wins. ‘Cannot’ is absolute unless explicitly overridden; an ordinary card does not implicitly override it.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Precedence: ‘Card overrides Law’; ‘Cannot is absolute unless explicitly overridden.’

answers.answer: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order. A Marquise March's two moves form one compound action and may not be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: unclear simultaneous effects and attacker ordering; March is one compound action.

answers.answer: ‘At start’ effects happen before all other effects in that phase; ‘at end’ effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions; so ordinary Daylight actions cannot be taken after beginning that last step.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: definitions of at-start/at-end and last-step restriction.

answers.answer: Hand size is public but card contents are private; show or reveal a hand only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected, but the deck may not. Deals are non-binding, cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Cards: hand/deck/pile information; agreements and card transfer/consent.

answers.answer: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple cards of the same required suit. When instructed to give or discard non-bird-suit cards, birds must be treated as that suit and the instruction determines the number; non-birds cannot pay an explicit bird requirement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Cards: deck reshuffle and bird substitution rules.

answers.answer: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If instructed to place/take/remove more pieces than can be handled, do the maximum possible; you cannot voluntarily do fewer. A shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and it does not excuse the Eyrie's obligation to complete its Decree actions (failure causes Turmoil).
answers.evidence: Pieces are finite: ‘no proxies’; maximum possible; no voluntary shortfall; costs/prerequisites and Eyrie obligation remain.

answers.answer: Pieces placed normally come from supply or, for tracked pieces, the leftmost track space. Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces go to the rightmost empty track space. Items removed from the game are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering effects from those removals.
answers.evidence: Removed faction pieces and placement paragraph; Special Rules → Place/remove/replace; simultaneous removal timing.

answers.answer: Resolve a forced action as if the affected player chose it, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes the battle decisions.
answers.evidence: Special Rules → Force: forced actions preserve abilities/restrictions; affected player makes battle decisions.

answers.answer: An enemy cannot replace a piece in the Keep clearing in a way that places a piece there, because replacement requires legal removal and placement and the Keep placement ban still applies. Swap is distinct: it ignores move and place restrictions, unlike a move or place, which follows its ordinary restrictions.
answers.evidence: Place/remove/replace: replacement cannot bypass Keep placement ban; Swap ignores move/place restrictions.

answers.answer: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins; the current player is included in the tie ordering.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: simultaneous 30 VP tie-break wording.

answers.answer: Forests are adjacent to clearings touching them without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. In Winter, the river also divides forests, affecting adjacency for Slip. Fall has no special rules.
answers.evidence: Shared rules: forest definition and Winter river; setup states ‘Fall has no special rules.’

answers.answer: Marquise begins with 25 warriors and 8 wood in supply. Place the Keep in any corner; this is the starting clearing. Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, one workshop, and one recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.
answers.evidence: Marquise setup (6.3): supplies, Keep, warrior placements, initial buildings and track arrangement.

answers.answer: Eyrie supplies 20 warriors. Place one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and leave the others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Put the other six roosts on the roost track from right to left.
answers.evidence: Eyrie setup (7.3): corner, pieces, leader/Viziers, remaining roosts.

answers.answer: Alliance supplies 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from its three-card hand. It starts with no pieces on the map and no officers.
answers.evidence: Alliance setup (8.3): supply, board, Supporters, hand distinction, map/officers.

answers.answer: Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Each other faction's relationship marker starts at Indifferent. Take the character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins, and bags go face up on matching tracks; other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. (Hidden R-marked ruin items are not repeated here.)
answers.evidence: Vagabond setup (9.3): character, forest, quests, relationships and S-marked items.

answers.answer: Recommended minimum reach totals: 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base reach values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law also permits adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.
answers.evidence: Recommended faction mix (5.2): player-count totals and base reaches.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, place one wood at each sawmill (one per sawmill even if several share a clearing), limited by the eight-wood supply. In Evening, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard down to five.
answers.evidence: Marquise Birdsong wood; Marquise Evening draw/discard.

answers.answer: Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available and Marquise chooses among eligible recruiters where to place them.
answers.evidence: Marquise Recruit: once per turn; shortage means maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answers.answer: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of printed VP under Disdain for Trade. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade, so Builder scores the printed item VP. Other extra crafting-point effects still apply despite Disdain.
answers.evidence: Eyrie special rules: Disdain; Builder ignores it; other extra crafting-point effects apply.

answers.answer: Builder: Viziers in Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit must place two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; gets one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, scores one extra VP beyond normal removal points.
answers.evidence: Eyrie leader table lists columns and abilities.

answers.answer: No. With Charismatic, each Recruit must place two warriors instead of one. If only one warrior remains, that required Decree action cannot be fully completed, so the Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil; it cannot place one and count the action as complete.
answers.evidence: Charismatic Recruit requires two; any required Decree action not fully completed causes immediate Turmoil.

answers.answer: Guerrilla War does not bypass warrior caps; warrior caps still apply. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker uses the lower die.
answers.evidence: Alliance Guerrilla War: higher die to defending Alliance, attacker lower; caps still apply.

answers.answer: Alliance cannot craft from Supporters; crafting is from hand. Alliance may inspect its face-down Supporters. Supporters do not count as hand cards and do not count toward hand limit.
answers.evidence: Supporters are inspectable by Alliance, spendable only for suit, separate from hand and hand limit; Daylight crafting from hand.

answers.answer: No. All Revolts must be completed before starting Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, the Alliance cannot return to Revolt during that Birdsong, so newly placed sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong order explicitly bars returning to Revolt after spreading begins.

answers.answer: No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors of one other player in the chosen clearing; two warriors from each of two opponents do not meet that single-player threshold. Martial Law adds a matching supporter to Spread Sympathy's cost. Organize has no Martial Law cost.
answers.evidence: Spread Sympathy Martial Law: three warriors of one other player; Organize has no Martial Law cost.

answers.answer: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage; moving warriors into one does. Moving only the Vagabond pawn does not trigger it. If allied warriors accompany a Vagabond move into sympathy, their movement is warrior movement and triggers Outrage, requiring one matching card for that affected move.
answers.evidence: Outrage exclusions: placing and pawn-only movement do not trigger; allied warriors moved with pawn do trigger.

answers.answer: Alliance Evening operations are Move, Battle, Recruit, and Organize. Take up to the number of officers, in any order and repetition. Officers remain on the board; using an operation does not consume one. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus and discard down to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Evening operations table and draw timing.

answers.answer: The Vagabond pawn is not removed. An effect that removes all enemy pieces from its clearing instead damages three Vagabond items. This applies to Revolt as well as another enemy remove-all-pieces effect.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Pawn and items; Alliance Revolt specifies enemy Vagabond damages three items instead.

answers.answer: Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum in either attack or defense is the number of all undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. It is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Hits taken become item damage: one hit damages one chosen undamaged item; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Battle; Pawn and items damage rules.

answers.answer: Face-up tea, coins, and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each item track holds at most three. Exhausting an item that is on a track sends it to Satchel. Damaged items move to Damaged box without changing face, and damaged items cannot pay for actions even if face up. Repair moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea/coins/bags then go to their track if space. Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready track-type items move to tracks if able.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Pawn and items; Repair and forest Rest procedures.

answers.answer: Capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on the bag track. Count items in Satchel plus Damaged box; items on tracks do not count. Check capacity as the last Evening step, not immediately when gaining an item. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Evening capacity step states formula, included/excluded items, timing, and permanent removal.

answers.answer: Forest Rest does not refresh an undamaged exhausted item. Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able. Refresh is a Birdsong step that flips exhausted items (two per face-up tea already on Refresh track, then three); Refresh changes face, not damage status. Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its face.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Evening Rest; Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair.

answers.answer: Aid exhausts any one item and gives a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there; the recipient can be Hostile. No crafted item is required to perform Aid. Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items box face up, but this is optional and no available item is required to Aid. For a non-Hostile relationship, improve one space by aiding the faction as many times as printed between the current and next spaces in the same turn; one Aid counts toward only one improvement. At Allied, each further Aid scores two VP.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight Aid; Relationships relationship advancement and Allied scoring.

answers.answer: At Allied status, allied warriors may accompany Vagabond on moves to a clearing, with warriors from one Allied faction; they follow their own movement restrictions, including rule, and cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At the start of a battle as attacker, Vagabond may treat warriors of one Allied faction there as its own to attack a different enemy; they cannot be used to attack that ally itself. They count toward the rolled-hit cap with Vagabond's undamaged swords, and may be removed to take hits.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Relationships → Move with ally and Attack with ally.

answers.answer: At battle end, the ally becomes Hostile if Vagabond removed more allied warriors than items damaged in that battle. Equal numbers do not trigger Hostility. This is the special allied battle-loss timing and concerns taking hits from the other enemy; it is not the rule for attacking the ally.
answers.evidence: Attack with ally: comparison, timing at battle end, equality, and scope of exception.

answers.answer: No. The Vagabond pawn's current clearing suit must match all crafting icons, so one clearing cannot satisfy a mixed fox-and-rabbit requirement. The pawn may be activated repeatedly for further icons/craftings by exhausting more hammers despite the usual once-per-turn limit. A crafted item may immediately be taken face up into Satchel or its track, subject to supply.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Craft: one hammer per icon, pawn repeat exception, all icons must match current clearing, item may be taken immediately.

answers.answer: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items while keeping their faces, immediately ends Daylight, and begins Evening.
answers.evidence: Base character table: starting items and special actions/results.

answers.answer: When Explore takes the last item from a ruin, the ruin is removed and its building slot is freed. Ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin; ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed, and Explore is the stated procedure here.
answers.evidence: Explore: last item removes ruin and frees slot; shared rules say ruins removed only when explicitly allowed.

answers.answer: Coalition partners are not enemies, so they cannot be treated as enemies to attack. Coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition: ‘Coalition partners are not enemies’; no automatic Allied powers.

answers.answer: Assuming the battle is on Vagabond's own turn, the first warrior removed makes that previously non-Hostile faction Hostile and is exempt from Infamy. The second hostile warrior gives one Infamy VP. Removing the hostile building gives one normal removal VP plus one Infamy VP. Total for the described removals is three VP: two from the building and one from the second warrior; the first warrior scores no Infamy. If it is another player's turn, there is no Infamy and the building gives only its one removal VP. The question does not specify turn ownership, so the total depends on that condition.
answers.evidence: Hostile/Infamy: first warrior that causes Hostility excluded; hostile building/token gives two on own turn; no Infamy on another player's turn.

answers.answer: A destination with hostile buildings only costs one boot, because extra boot cost applies only when the destination has hostile warriors. A destination with hostile warriors from several factions still costs one extra boot total: the rule says one extra if there are any warriors of any Hostile faction, not per faction. Thus both destinations cost one base boot, with only the warriors destination requiring a second boot.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Move: one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; not buildings/tokens.

answers.answer: No. Taking an available dominance card puts it into hand; activating it is a separate choice/action in the player's own Daylight at the required VP. Taking and activating dominance do not require a Marquise faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Dominance: taking and activation are separate; neither requires faction action allowance.

answers.answer: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.
answers.evidence: Components: ‘Faction-piece ownership cannot change’; items are not faction pieces; possession does not confer ownership.

answers.answer: An immediate-effect card is resolved and discarded; an item card requires the item in map supply, and the taker scores its listed VP subject to Eyrie's exception. A persistent-effect card stays in the play area and its text applies; identical persistent effects cannot be crafted twice. A card in the play area is outside the hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
answers.evidence: Craft: Immediate effect and Persistent effect paragraphs.

answers.answer: Ambush cards cannot be crafted; a defender may play one for two immediate hits, or an attacker may use a matching one to foil a defending ambush. Dominance cards also cannot be crafted; activate one to change the victory condition or spend one for suit.
answers.evidence: Craft: ‘Ambush cards cannot be crafted’ and ‘Dominance cards cannot be crafted’ with permitted uses.

answers.answer: Randomly determine starting player and seating. Take faction boards and their listed pieces; choose Fall or Winter. Put score markers at 0; battle dice are placed nearby. Factions set up in letter order (Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond), which is distinct from turn order; turns proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 2, 6, 7; Turn Structure says clockwise turns.

answers.answer: The first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn. They need not finish the action, phase, or turn first.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn.’

answers.answer: To initiate battle, choose a clearing where you have warriors or a pawn and an enemy is present as defender. You do not need to rule the clearing.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3): choose clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy; battle does not require rule.

answers.answer: For applicable before-roll or after-roll battle effects when both sides have effects at that timing, the attacker chooses their order. At the same timing more generally, attacker chooses battle effect order. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its own pieces.
answers.evidence: Battle steps 2, 4, 6: attacker orders both timing groups; removing side orders its removal-trigger effects.

answers.answer: In Count Hits, add extra hits (which are not capped by warriors) and subtract ignored hits from the total.
answers.evidence: Battle step 5: ‘Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits.’

answers.answer: When a non-Vagabond faction crafts an item card, the item must be in the map item supply; take it from that supply into Crafted Items. The ordinary VP reward is the amount printed on the card, subject to Eyrie's Disdain exception (one VP, except Builder ignores Disdain). Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as the Vagabond does.
answers.evidence: Craft immediate-effect item rule: item comes from supply into Crafted Items; scores listed VP; Eyrie exception.

answers.answer: Eyrie activates roosts for crafting; Alliance activates sympathy. A crafting piece's suit is the suit of its clearing. A three-color question mark accepts any suit.
answers.evidence: Craft (4.1): faction crafting pieces, piece suit, and three-color question mark.

answers.answer: Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, subject to Supporters capacity. During Alliance Daylight, Craft, Mobilize, and Train may be done in any order and any number; Alliance need not finish all crafting before Mobilizing or Training.
answers.evidence: Alliance Daylight: any order and number; Mobilize procedure and Supporters cap.

answers.answer: In Evening, score VP shown on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus and discard to five. This full normal Evening still occurs after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Evening and Turmoil paragraphs explicitly retain score/draw/discard after Turmoil.

answers.answer: To initiate its Daylight Battle action, Vagabond exhausts one sword. An exhausted but undamaged sword cannot pay that cost because action costs require a face-up undamaged item. It still counts toward Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum, which counts all undamaged swords whether face up or face down.
answers.evidence: Vagabond item rule requires face-up undamaged item to exhaust; Battle cost and sword hit cap specify face-down undamaged swords count.

answers.answer: A turn proceeds Birdsong, then Daylight, then Evening. Turns are clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise begins their Birdsong.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: phase order; ‘Take turns clockwise.’

answers.answer: Each hit damages one undamaged Vagabond item of the Vagabond's choice; it goes to the Damaged box without changing whether it is face up or face down. A damaged item cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored if no undamaged items remain.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Pawn and items: damage moves item without face change; one hit per undamaged item; excess ignored.
